posts.caption: Four words. No new apps. Audit → Eliminate → Automate → Integrate. Do step 1 tonight — it takes five minutes and it's the first time most people actually see the noise. Save this and send it to the friend who's always 'so behind'.

Your first AI prompt, word for word: 'Explain this to me in plain words and tell me exactly what I need to do.' Paste any confusing email or letter above it. That's the whole lesson. You're not behind — nobody showed you.
Most people aren't stuck because they're broken. They're stuck because nobody ever showed them how simple it actually is. I'm Ian. I'm The Translator. More soon.

How to clean up your Gmail inbox without deleting anything: open one newsletter, tap the three dots, 'Filter messages like this', tick Skip the Inbox, send it to a folder called Later. Five senders tonight. Tomorrow your inbox is just people. Outlook users — 'Rules' does the same thing; comment if you want that version. Save this for tonight.
posts.caption_fb: I'm going to save some of you an hour a day. Your inbox isn't full, it's unsorted — the school email is buried under thirty shops and newsletters. Open one newsletter, tap the three dots, choose 'Filter messages like this', tick 'Skip the Inbox' and send it to a folder called Later. Do it for five senders tonight. Tomorrow morning your inbox is just people. Nothing deleted, nothing lost — it's just quiet. If you're on Outlook say so below and I'll do that version.

posts.caption: The attention tax: dozens of tiny interruptions that cost nothing each and everything together. Reactive living versus proactive simplicity. Tonight: which notifications earned the right to interrupt you? Mute the rest. Send this to someone who's 'always busy'.

Capable but invisible is not the same as behind. Your skill is fine — it just never got translated into the online world. That part's learnable, and it's simpler than anyone told you. Send this to the most underrated person you know.

Decoded is open for founding members.
